headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Goose’s filesystem/MCP tooling into Khoj’s retrieval and broad network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while Khoj reads indexed documents and personal notes. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Goose writes attacker-controlled text into shared files that Khoj later ingests. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so I choose medium over low because the shared filesystem is explicit.
conditions: IF Goose writes prompt-like text into a file that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj treats retrieved document text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Separate Goose workspaces from Khoj-indexed folders
Disable automatic indexing of active coding directories
Add a provenance banner to retrieved notes before reuse
Review MCP sources before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering between file writes and retrieval

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose handles source code, files in cwd, and secrets such as model provider keys, while Khoj indexes personal notes/documents and can call configured search providers or a cloud/self-hosted server. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive code or notes can flow into Khoj’s retrieval and then out through its networked search/API surfaces. The default overlap makes leakage materially plausible.
conditions: IF Goose and Khoj share a directory or synced notes folder
IF Khoj indexes files containing secrets or private notes
IF Khoj sends retrieved content to external search or cloud services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any Khoj-indexed path
Use separate OS accounts or home subfolders
Turn off external search providers in Khoj
Exclude code repositories from Khoj ingestion
requires-engineering: add per-folder allowlists and redaction before indexing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its shared state is via filesystem. Khoj has read_filesystem and a shared index across clients, so concurrent access to the same files or notes can create write/read conflicts even though Khoj cannot write files. This is a real overlap in mutable resources, but not the highest-risk git-lock scenario.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or notes directory
IF Goose modifies files while Khoj is indexing or reading them
mitigations: Run them on separate working copies
Pause Khoj indexing during Goose edits
Avoid letting Goose edit files that Khoj serves live
Use git branches for Goose changes
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can produce tool-driven outputs from files and MCP sources, and Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that may present those outputs back to the user. If Khoj treats Goose-generated text as authoritative without verification, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into downstream answers. The pairwise pathway exists in default workflows, but there is no evidence of autonomous action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Khoj uses Goose-generated notes or transcripts as source material
IF Khoj answers without verifying Goose-produced claims
mitigations: Mark Goose outputs as untrusted in Khoj
Require source links for any retrieved claim
Spot-check high-impact answers before sharing
Keep Goose transcripts separate from canonical notes
requires-engineering: add verification and citation scoring

E_compliance.rationale: Goose touches source code, files in cwd, and secrets, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and may use cloud or self-hosted search providers. If regulated or private data is placed in shared indexed content, retention and residency obligations can diverge between the two systems. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj routes queries or snippets to external providers
IF retention policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Khoj indexes
Use self-hosted-only modes where possible
Document retention settings for both tools
Separate personal notes from work repositories
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows
